analysis.investment_thesis: Exato is a small IT-enabled services company outside my circle — not a consumer-facing compounder, and its balance sheet has deteriorated with borrowings jumping from INR 6 Cr to INR 28 Cr in two years. At P/E 35x with erratic cash flows and D/E of 0.56, this fails my conservative tests on multiple fronts.
key_strengths: Decent ROE 28.2% and ROCE 26.5% indicate capital productivity at current scale
Revenue growth from INR 73 Cr to INR 124 Cr (30% CAGR) shows demand traction
Net profit doubled from INR 5 Cr to INR 10 Cr in FY25
key_risks: Debt-to-Equity of 0.56 (28/50) well above my 0.3 ceiling — borrowings nearly 5x in two years
P/E 35x is rich for a INR 338 Cr micro-cap IT services firm with FY24 FCF of -INR 20 Cr
Promoter holding only 54.73% — borderline, and IT services is outside my consumer-retail circle of competence
red_flags: Aggressive borrowing-funded expansion: borrowings up from INR 6 Cr to INR 28 Cr
FY24 Operating CF of -INR 14 Cr and FCF of -INR 20 Cr signal working capital stress
Financing CF of INR 19 Cr in FY25 indicates growth funded externally, not internally
analysis.detailed_analysis:
This is not a business I would look at. I build conviction in boring, predictable, consumer-facing franchises — DMart, branded FMCG, quality private banks — where demand is steady and cash compounds quietly. Exato is a 2016-incorporated IT-enabled services micro-cap where revenue jumped from INR 73 Cr to INR 124 Cr while borrowings rose from INR 6 Cr to INR 28 Cr and FY24 produced operating cash flow of -INR 14 Cr. The profit line is positive, but cumulative FCF over three years is barely zero — that is not earnings quality I trust.

At INR 338 Cr market cap and 35x earnings, I am paying a premium multiple for a sub-scale services business with rising finance costs (INR 1 Cr to INR 2 Cr), D/E of 0.56, and limited operating history. Promoter holding at 54.73% is at my lower bound. ROE of 28% is attractive on paper, but ROEs in small IT services are notoriously unstable as attrition, client concentration and wage inflation bite. I would pass and watch for five more years of disciplined execution before revisiting.
